A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MILR work. All 21 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A.1–A.4, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MILR evaluations on GenEval, T2I-CompBench and WISE, together with quantitative ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds reward-model results for T2I-CompBench and WISE in appendix Tables 7–8.

M1.justification: The latent policy-gradient procedure, frozen Janus-Pro model, prefix optimization and Appendix A.1 algorithm variants are unchanged. Figure 2's added explanation of prompt-conditioned rewards restates the existing formulation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GenEval, T2I-CompBench and WISE. The new reward-model tables reuse existing tasks and domains; WISE's category breakdown does not establish additional dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the main and efficiency comparisons is unchanged. The added reward tables extend the existing SelfReward, GPT-4o, UnifiedReward, MixedReward and benchmark-evaluator reward comparison to two further benchmarks, without introducing a distinct comparator.

E3.justification: v2 newly reports non-oracle reward-feedback conditions for MILR on T2I-CompBench and WISE, supplementing their oracle-reward evaluations. Existing splits, metrics, model sizes and optimization hyperparameters remain unchanged; no rerunning of existing experiments is established.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3.2 extends the existing analysis of sensitivity to reward-model choice from GenEval to T2I-CompBench and WISE. Modality ablations, optimization-strategy comparisons, token-ratio studies, efficiency analysis and error cases are retained.

E5.justification: Section 4.3.1 retains three-seed averaging, and Figure 5's variability displays are unchanged. The added tables report point scores without introducing run counts, confidence intervals or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Tables 7–8 add reward-dependent scores and category breakdowns. MixedReward and GPT-4o score 0.5043 and 0.4775 on T2I-CompBench, but 0.49 and 0.52 on WISE, respectively. These are newly reported conditions; existing main results and GenEval reward scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the mathematical formulation of latent optimization and the appendix algorithms are unchanged. No new assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about joint image-text latent reasoning, test-time operation without parameter updates, benchmark performance and temporal/cultural reasoning.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, failure modes and limitations concerning autoregressive models and reward quality remain unchanged. Appendix A.3.2 retains its MixedReward interpretation without discussing GPT-4o's higher WISE score in the added table.

D1.justification: v1's Reproducibility Statement promises a future code release. v2 removes that statement and supplies project and code links on the title page. Hyperparameters, hardware and efficiency disclosures remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish the linked repository's contents.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to prior research are unchanged. Reference-list differences concern URL spacing and line wrapping.

P1.justification: Local edits clarify Figure 2's caption, add table references in Appendix A.3.2 and remove the short Reproducibility Statement. The main narrative and section sequence are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7–8, refines Figure 2's image-token grouping and caption, and reflows appendix content. The unchanged efficiency table becomes Table 9 and moves within page 21. Existing plots and qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: Tables 7–8 provide useful evidence about non-oracle rewards beyond GenEval, and the new code/project pointers improve reproducibility information. The benefit is limited by incomplete integration: Appendix A.3.2 retains its MixedReward-best interpretation despite WISE favoring GPT-4o, 0.52 versus 0.49. The central method and headline evidence remain unchanged.
